text:
[LSER.6.6.1] The aggregation names are reserved words
([LLEX.9.5]) and carry rows on [LLEX.9.6]. An author must not
declare a slot under one of them, and the compiler must refuse
such a declaration at schema / series declaration time.

The reservation is **unconditional**. It does not depend on the
schema having a declared series, and a slot named `mean` is
refused whether or not one exists.

What makes these names reservable at all is a collision rather
than a position argument: [LSER.6]'s companion form
`cursor.<agg>` is syntactically identical to a slot read, so an
author-declared slot and the aggregation occupy one position and
one must yield. Conditioning the refusal on a series is what
made adding a series to a schema retroactively illegalise a slot
declared elsewhere, which is the action at a distance the single
list exists to remove.
